boundary_note: Bounded first pass for the frozen Totopotomoy Creek record (May 28-30, 1864) in Grant's Overland Campaign [May-June 1864]. Haw's Shop (VA058, May 28) and Old Church (VA059, May 30) are separate cavalry records inside these dates, and Cold Harbor (VA062) begins on May 31. Campaign-wide marches, captures, returns, reinforcements and multi-action loss totals are context; they are not assigned to one record or added across records. Draft claims do not alter model inputs.

claims.rationale: No inspected return establishes matched personnel at a common opening boundary. The frozen side-specific numerical strength bounds are blank (missing_numeric_strength). No figure in this pass is adopted as a simultaneous opening force.

claims.rationale: Formations named without counts. None is adopted as a matched opening strength; live zeros are not measured absence.

claims.value: The frozen result reads Inconclusive and the live result Indecisive. NPS says the II Corps took the first line of trenches but was stopped at the main line, and that the V Corps was driven back to Shady Grove Road after heavy fighting near Bethesda Church. Humphreys says the attacking brigade was driven back but the enemy's resolute attack was then repulsed, and relays Warren that the enemy had abandoned the field by ten o'clock.
claims.rationale: Retain the original result and engagement interval; later movements and campaign contribution are different measures. No new probabilities or individual causal credit. NPS and Humphreys describe the Bethesda Church outcome differently.

claims.value: The frozen casualty text reads 2,200 (US 1,100; CS 1,100); the live field reads 1,890 (US 731; CS 1,159). Humphreys gives, for the period after crossing the Pamunkey and before June 1, 1,622 wounded, 400 killed and about 1,000 missing, and thinks Confederate losses to the morning of June 1 were probably nearly equal to the Union's.
claims.rationale: Original casualty returns were not inspected; preserve totals, categories, cutoffs and differences. No canonical reconciliation or casualty-based opening count; related actions must not be added without resolving population overlap. Humphreys' figures span May 28–31 and include Haw's Shop and Old Church; they are not assigned here.

open_questions: Warren's, Hancock's and Early's reports, Lee's dispatches and the returns remain deferred. Doles's death on June 2 (NPS) falls in Cold Harbor's interval.

NPS/CWSAC (the live NPS page and the frozen Arnold rows) is one family. Humphreys' The Virginia Campaign of ’64 and ’65 (1883) is an interested history by the Army of the Potomac's chief of staff, in the same author family as the registered From Gettysburg to the Rapidan, and it shares headquarters papers with Meade's and Sheridan's reports. Meade's, Sheridan's, Hampton's, Butler's and Wild's reports, printed in Official Records Series I, Volume XXXVI, Parts 1 and 2, are separate families of interested commanders' accounts; the volume is a shared container, not an additional witness. Report dates are not event times or proof of contemporary knowledge.
No automatic commander attribution, causal campaign score, morale/readiness number or battle/campaign double counting.
